dossiers.title: Myth of Empires
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 9 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The core experience is open-ended survival and settlement building, using resource gathering, crafting, farming, animal taming and commandable workers or troops rather than a fixed linear campaign.
Players describe broad proficiency and crafting systems, but raising those skills can require extensive, repeated harvesting and other routine labor.
Territory conflict and guild-scale coordination are a prominent path, while players also report viable slower solo or PvE homestead play with recruitable NPC assistance.
Some players report that ongoing worker provisions and settlement upkeep create a time-intensive routine and make extended breaks from play inconvenient.
The ability to build a homestead, tame creatures and connect crafting, cultivation and military systems is a recurring appeal of the sandbox.
Complaints about unresponsive melee hit detection and awkward fight feedback recur in accounts describing hand-to-hand encounters.
Russian-language reviews written in 2024 criticized awkward interface translation and item search labels; they do not establish the present quality of the localization.
Dated 2024 Russian reviews described optimization, server-selection and creature-interaction bugs; the reports are historical player experiences, not independently verified current issues.
Player experiences differ substantially between peaceful gathering and building and competitive guild-driven territory activity, with some reports criticizing the relative support for PvE content.

conflicts.statement: Players disagree about whether solo and PvE pursuits provide satisfying independent goals or are overshadowed by systems primarily directed toward PvP competition.

dossiers.title: Card Shark
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The central activity is carrying out card-table scams through observed gestures, manipulation and short trick-specific mini-games, not playing a traditional collectible or tactical card game.
The story introduces new deception procedures in quick succession, with advancement tied more to learning fresh sleights than to upgrading a persistent character build.
Timing, remembering multistep moves and controlling precise gestures are the central execution challenges; more elaborate tricks become demanding for some players.
Some players find the ongoing cycle of learning instructions and immediately executing short tricks repetitive, especially when later remembering sequences without a convenient practice option.
Scams propel a scripted intrigue among figures in eighteenth-century France; its narrative pacing and staged encounters differ from free exploration or open-ended gambling.
Distinctive hand-drawn art, theatrical staging and period-inspired music are notable recurring positives that lend personality to the deception narrative.
Control feedback is divided: players praise hands-on interaction but some find mouse or controller motions finicky and stressful during complicated tricks.
A 2022 Russian review reported occasional glitches during the card-trick sequences; this dated report does not verify any ongoing technical condition.

conflicts.statement: Some players celebrate fresh tactile puzzles and theatrical intrigue, while others find the tightly guided and repeatedly tutorialized trick sequences too restrictive.

dossiers.title: Eternights
dossiers.summary: Evidence summary: 8 validated structured observations; consult observations and conflicts for supported findings.

observations.statement: The game alternates realtime action battles and dungeon passages with dating-style relationships, making combat and character interaction two linked parts of one short adventure.
A calendar-like arrangement of expeditions and social meetings resembles social-simulation RPGs, but the development and total campaign are markedly more compact than larger genre examples.
Players discuss a combat rhythm of dodging, parrying and charging attacks against shielded enemies, while opinions about its responsiveness and depth vary.
Reviews criticize repetitive fight patterns, modest mechanical evolution and required replays of tutorials or story sequences when attempting another route.
The relationships, character banter, expressive performances and romantic decisions are praised as meaningful reasons to continue the apocalyptic plot.
Opinions on the concise story and its ending diverge: some feel engaged with emotional scenes, others see a rushed structure or insufficient resolution.
Some enjoy learning dodge/parry windows and aggressive shield-breaking tactics, but others report defensive enemy designs or quick-time action as repetitive friction.
Russian-language community participants requested subtitles before launch in June 2023; those historical requests do not verify today's availability or quality of Russian localization.

conflicts.statement: Players' combat accounts range from rewarding parry-and-dodge exchanges to thin or repetitive action that interrupts their preferred character story.
Some praise the emotional character-led narrative, whereas others criticize the late-story pacing and ending.
